newsitem.title: UK: Base metals end on positive note on LME.
newsitem.headline: Base metals end on positive note on LME.

text.p: Copper and aluminium built on a healthy early bounce and ended near the day's highs on Wednesday as the market's tone brightened.
"They've countered some of the negative sentiment of yesterday. But they're not out of danger yet," said analyst Robin Bhar of brokers Brandeis.
The rest of the base metals on the London Metal Exchange (LME) were also boosted higher as short covering and speculative buying lifted sagging prices.
Aluminium ended the afternoon kerb $8 firmer at $1,555 per tonne, having snapped up from support at $1,535 early in the day.
That close above $1,550 signalled a chance for consolidation after four days of sharp falls, analysts said.
"It was probably overdone yesterday and today's close is positive," Bhar said.
"But it's difficult to know whther this correction has further to go with the charts still weak and sentiment bearish."
Copper trundled higher after support at the important $2,200 area held despite protracted tests, traders said.
It ended the afternoon kerb at the important $2,250 level, an increase of $38 from Tuesday, and just below the day's high of $2,555.
Chartwise the close should help relieve downward pressure and provide support, analysts said.
Instrumental to copper's bounce was the continued tightness of the cash/threes backwardation amid renewed borrowing and cash buying in the rings.
The spread was narrower than on Tuesday at $115/$125 but on par with the morning's levels.
"It looked at one point like it was going to go to $80/$90. But it didn't, and there wasn't any aggressive selling in the ring," Bhar said.
Zinc, which has been resilient and well bid despite weakness in the other metals, held within recent price levels.
It finished at $1,186, up $10, after it turned back at $1,193 without reaching the psychological $1,200 level.
Nickel ended a sizeable $150 firmer at $7,880 as fund interest combined with strength in the other metals underpinned the market.
Lead was up $5 at $649, helped by trade short covering. Tin was also up $15 at $5,935.
